description: SPS continues work on its responsible AI roadmap.
SPS hosts public data destruction and recycling March 5.
Officers organized a winter clothing drive for residents.
Chief attended community events and justice discussions.

chips.text: Commissioner asked about SaskPolytech program's role in policing careers.
Chief attended Afrocentric Symposium panel on justice and community trust.

description: Police Traffic Unit issued 15,000 tickets in 2025.
Mandatory alcohol screening at traffic stops well-received.
School zone photo enforcement tickets increased.

chips.text: Chief McBride noted traffic stops often uncover other criminal activity like drug trafficking.
Motorists benefit from increased road safety and reduced criminal activity.
Reason for drop in out-of-province red light camera tickets is unknown.
SPS expects to improve traffic unit staffing levels through new hiring.

speakers.name: Tony Landry
said: Presented 2025 annual reports for Traffic Unit and Combined Traffic Services.
Detailed enforcement efforts, including 15,000 tickets and impaired driving increase.
Discussed staffing challenges and commitment to road safety education.

description: Renews Saskatoon's $5,652.00 membership in the Canadian Association of Police Governance.

chips.text: Council discussed hosting the 2027 CAPG conference, noting Saskatoon hosted in 2022.
Saskatoon taxpayers fund the annual $5,652.00 membership fee.
